source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Carrollton campus publishes 45 MW of IT capacity, enough at typical AI training densities for roughly 4,400 to 8,800 H100-equivalent accelerators, making it one of the few Texas sites with disclosed power.

The 45 MW figure is a published IT load, not total building power, and it translates to roughly 1,100 racks at 40 kW per rack. That scale supports substantial AI training or inference but is not the largest published in Texas. The 600,000 square feet of technical space gives room for that density, but the operator does not publish actual rack counts or accelerator inventory.

In Texas, this campus ranks third by published capacity and accounts for 9.5 percent of the state's 475 MW of disclosed data center IT load. Only 19 of 133 mapped Texas facilities publish power figures, so most of the state's actual compute capacity is undisclosed. That makes any ranking provisional and means the grid constraint cannot be assessed from published figures alone.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, ISO 27001, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, qualify the building for regulated enterprise workloads, but none are specific to AI. The operator does not publish tenants, so the certifications indicate what the space could host, not what it currently runs. The suitability score of 71 reflects published capacity and operator type, and its missing input is an announced expansion, so it says little about whether this campus will grow.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
